title.narrative: Guinea Natural Resources, Mining and Environmental Management Project

description.narrative: Guinea holds an exceptional wealth of natural resources, including vast mineral deposits and some of West Africa's most ecologically significant forests and protected areas. As the country advances large-scale economic development — most notably the Simandou iron-ore project — it faces mounting pressure to manage the trade-offs between extractive growth and the long-term value of its natural capital for environmental services, human well-being, and social resilience. With an initial financing of US$65 million — comprising an IDA Credit of US$32.5 million and an IDA Grant of US$32.5 million — bringing the total operation to US$82.53 million with the Additional Financing, this project supports the Ministry of Mining and Geology (MMG) and the Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development (MESD) in strengthening the institutional, regulatory, and governance frameworks needed to navigate these trade-offs sustainably. Both ministries have undertaken significant reforms, and the project is designed to align with and reinforce these efforts — building capacity, consolidating institutional frameworks, and improving governance across the mining and environment sectors. This project is among the first in Guinea to apply the Environment and Social Framework (ESF), which also serves as a guiding instrument for strengthening the national environmental and social management system.The Additional Financing of US$17,530,685 — sourced from PROGREEN (US$8 million), the SCALE Trust Fund (US$7 million), and the Global Biodiversity Framework Fund (US$2.53 million) — deepens and scales up the project's contribution to its Development Objective: to strengthen institutional capacities for integrated management of mineral and natural resources in Guinea and enhance benefits from the mining and environment sectors. It does so through three mutually reinforcing areas of intervention. First, it operationalizes the Guinea Conservation Trust Fund (CTF) as a sustainable financing mechanism for conservation, targeting up to US$100 million in mobilized capital, and thereby providing a durable institutional foundation for long-term natural resource management. Second, it expands protected area management and community livelihoods across new strategic landscapes — including the Fouta Djallon Highlands, the Gambia–Faleme Faunal Reserve, and the Pinselly–Soyah National Park — directly increasing the area under enhanced management to 4.8 million hectares and creating 6,550 jobs for women and youth. Third, it advances Guinea's readiness for a Forest Emission Reductions Program through a national MRV strategy, a Benefit Sharing Plan, and carbon rights regulatory support, unlocking access to climate finance and an estimated 18 million carbon credits. Together, these investments strengthen both the institutional architecture and the on-the-ground delivery needed to achieve the PDO, while extending the project closing date to June 30, 2029.Component A — Improve the Institutional Framework for Mining and Environment. This component harmonizes regulations and enhances coordination between MMG and MEDD. It supports the alignment of mining and environment regulatory frameworks (A1), and develops intersectoral coordination tools (A2). The additional financing scales up sub-component A2 by operationalizing the Guinea CTF, including its governance structures, capitalization strategy, and dedicated windows for AIGAs, the Fouta Djallon landscape, and Forest MRV. Sub-component A3, which strengthens Guinea's capacity on global climate commitments, remains unchanged.Component B — Mining Policies, Institutions, Governance, and Economic Integration. Unchanged by the additional financing, this component upgrades mining sector governance and institutional capacity. It supports regulatory reform and resource access (B1), and promotes local content, SME participation in mining supply chains, and citizen engagement mechanisms (B2).Component C — Environmental and Natural Resources Management. This component strengthens MEDD's capacity to manage Guinea's environmental assets. Sub-component C1 is expanded to support a national Forest MRV strategy, a Strategic Environmental and Social Assessment, a Benefit Sharing Plan, and carbon rights regulatory advisory services. Sub-component C2 scales up protected area management through the CTF sinking fund, extending coverage to new landscapes and financing community-led agroforestry and restoration activities to reduce pressure on conservation zones and support local livelihoods.Component D — Project Management. This component finances PIU operations, including procurement, financial management, environmental and social oversight, and monitoring and evaluation
The Development Objective is to strengthen institutional capacities for integrated management of mineral and natural resources in Guinea and enhanced benefits from the mining and environment sectors.

title.narrative: Score for reform of the legal and regulatory framework and dissemination

comment.narrative:
This indicator should capture the progress of regulatory reforms underway in the natural resources and environmental management sector. It refers to five specific laws and related regulations. Advancement in the reform of each Code will be assessed by the following score: 0= No law existing / 1= Drafted law or law to be revised / 2= Law adopted / 3= Law adopted and related regulation drafted / 4= Law and related regulation adopted and disseminated The indicator global score will be the addition of each Code score
